title: Android file permission issues
author: hikari-no-yume
body: As exemplified by https://github.com/touchHLE/touchHLE/issues/392, we have had repeated reports of Android users managing to copy files to touchHLE_apps, but them not showing up due to incorrect UNIX permissions. Certain methods of copying files don't seem to cause this problem. We don't know what causes this or if it's in our power to fix it, but maybe we can. It would be good to at least understand why it's happening.

comments.author: acieslewicz
comments.body:
Some extra info. It seems certain file managers actually move original file which preserves the media_rw group, while others seem to do a pseudo copy (which changes the group). This seems to prevent the app from interacting with the file due to the scoped file permissions. Given file management is restricted on non rooted devices, I'm not sure there is anything we can do internally to fix this silently. I did try creating a shadow copy of the ipa and that doesn't work. Perhaps there is a solution out there but I don't know enough about Android to implement it.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59a0bb7e-8793-4d8e-92aa-9b9285506dd2)

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body:
@acieslewicz This is very useful, thank you! That finally makes it start to make sense, I hadn't considered that somehow the UID and GID could be wrong, not just the permissions. Why is this even possible…

I assume you reproduced this on your own device? If so, I would really appreciate it if you could try a few things:

- Can you try adding some code (on the _Rust_ side; have a look at `paths.rs`, that's probably the right place to hack something in) that does a `chmod` or `chown` on these files?
- Can you try (again on the Rust side) setting the setuid and setgid bits on the `touchHLE_apps` directory? _If_ that works, I think it would mean that future copies/moves into the directory would inherit the correct UID/GID.

comments.author: acieslewicz
comments.body:
Did a bit more poking around. So the uid of the ipa doesn't matter just the gid. I attempted to use chown in order to change the group on the file (operation is not permitted). I attempted to change the group of the parent folder which worked but didn't solve the access issue for the IPA (I think this is because we already own the folder). I also tried to run a shell command to copy the file, but I get a permission denied error. It seems we can't really interact with files that have the media_rw group.

From some extra poking around I did it seems that the File app that works provides access via the storage access framework while zarchiver doesn't? I'm happy to test any ideas as needed.

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body: @acieslewicz Can you chmod the folder to set the setgid bit though?

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body:
Oh I had somehow missed that, in the screenshot, the setgid bit is already set. Damn.

I guess this is just a bug in Android that we can't fix. :(

I'll remove the milestone…
